record: AISEF V2 — C2-P5 correction, LANE-P5C independent audit (reviewer report) and its reconciliation
authority: owner ruling 2026-09-30 (P5 CORRECTION AUTHORIZED): LANE-P5C read-only audit of requirement coverage, plan-only overconstraint, multi-facet criteria, polarity, synthetic approval authority and probe expressiveness
nature: a read-only subagent's report over the repository at 0f77995 (it wrote only its report); a reviewer's opinion, NOT evidence of product behaviour — every behavioural claim of the P5 correction rests on P5-FALSIFIABILITY.json

method.neutral: A spec is neutral when EVERY implementation conforming to the frozen requirements satisfies it, whatever it chose for the open choices; interface assumptions (IA-*) are listed where a library spec needs one.
method.requirement_clause_classes: NORMATIVE_PRODUCT_REQUIREMENT: a testable product obligation; UNSUPPORTED_FOR_FULL_ENFORCEMENT: normative but outside every probe's vocabulary whatever is assumed (durability, crashes, locks, code structure, file-access tracing, interpreter version, documentation); ENGINEERING_TEST_REQUIREMENT: obligations on the developer test suite; DESCRIPTIVE: purpose/non-goal prose measured elsewhere.
method.plan_criterion_rule: NORMATIVE when every asserted clause traces to a frozen clause and the only non-normative content is the call shape/return representation used to state it; PLAN_ONLY_DETAIL when it asserts any behaviour or artefact the requirements do not require (plan module/helper, stream contents, exception attributes, a fixed open choice, flags) or contradicts them — normative clauses are then listed separately; ENGINEERING_TEST_REQUIREMENT when its subject is the developer test suite/coverage/runners; UNSUPPORTED_FOR_FULL_ENFORCEMENT when its core clause is normative but unobservable.

key_gaps: No neutral spec for the hash formula (R-3.2/3), the GENESIS value (R-3.2/5: a disjunction), first_bad_index (R-3.3/4), snapshot content/order/--out identity (R-6/1-2, R-6/4), CLI conflict exit 4 (R-9/5) and CLI apply success (R-5/5, R-14/3): each presumes an open choice (encoding, representation, layout, batch file format).
Byte identity of a product-written pre-state is not expressible (equals_before anchors after the workspace step); only line_count/jsonl fields are.
Library verify verdicts are never neutral (representation); the neutral verify is the CLI exit code 0/5, which cannot witness R-3.4's same-instance clause.
Neutral library specs still need IA-1 (Ledger(path)), IA-2 (apply_batch with JSON lists for tuples), IA-4, IA-5, IA-9, IA-10; 'same result' additionally needs IA-8/IA-14.
Durability, crash atomicity, the lock, file-access confinement and in-memory independence are UNSUPPORTED_FOR_FULL_ENFORCEMENT.

normative_clauses.note: restated in R-6, R-9, R-14

normative_clauses.note: non-goal; measurable half is R-12/1

normative_clauses.note: non-goal; its measurable half is the socket prohibition R-12/1

normative_clauses.note: non-goal; measured through R-10/2 (sqlite3 is outside the allowlist) and R-3.2/1

normative_clauses.clause: No client/server split. This is a single-process library + CLI.
No third-party runtime dependencies (no cryptography, no pynacl, no requests).
normative_clauses.note: subsumed by R-10/2 (allowlist)

normative_clauses.clause: All keys are normalized to Unicode NFC before any storage, lookup, hashing, or serialization step.
open_choices: where normalisation happens (entry point, helper name)
whether a non-str key is refused

normative_clauses.clause: Two strings that differ only in NFC/NFD representation MUST be treated as the same key.
Equivalence is checked using unicodedata.normalize("NFC", s).
open_choices: spelling of the call (module attribute vs from-import)
normative_clauses.note: mechanism directive; its behavioural consequence is R-3.1/1-2

normative_clauses.clause: Comparison of the normalized form MUST be byte-exact.
normative_clauses.note: no case folding, no NFKC: 'k' vs 'K' and U+FB01 vs 'fi' are different keys

normative_clauses.clause: The ledger is a single JSONL file.
open_choices: whether a mutation on a missing file creates it
line terminator (\n assumed by R-7)
whether an existing empty file is a valid empty ledger

normative_clauses.clause: Each line is one of: { op: put, key, value, ts, id } / { op: delete, key, ts, id }
open_choices: field order
whitespace / escaping (ensure_ascii)
whether extra fields are allowed
whether a delete line may carry value
who supplies ts (caller vs implementation)

normative_clauses.clause: Each line carries a "hash" field ... computed over the canonical bytes of the line with "hash" and "prev_hash" set to the empty string: hash = SHA-256( prev_hash || "|" || canonical_bytes )
open_choices: canonical-bytes encoding (key order, separators, non-ASCII escaping, number form, UTF-8)
byte encoding of the prev_hash operand and of '|'
digest text encoding (lower/upper hex, other)
whether the prev_hash operand at verify time is the stored field or the previous line's stored hash

normative_clauses.clause: prev_hash of the next line = this hash
The first line's prev_hash is the literal string "GENESIS" (64 hex chars of zeros OR the literal string "GENESIS" — implementation choice ...)
open_choices: GENESIS form: literal "GENESIS" or 64 '0' characters (explicitly the implementer's)

normative_clauses.clause: but it MUST be documented and constant
open_choices: where it is documented (README, docs/, docstring)
normative_clauses.note: 'documented' has no location and no content rule; 'constant' is a property across ledgers, which no probe compares

normative_clauses.clause: The chain is append-only: existing records MUST NOT be rewritten in place.
normative_clauses.note: R-5 rewrites the whole file through temp+rename; 'in place' is read as: the old records' bytes survive

normative_clauses.clause: Any modification to a committed line (mutating value, swapping op, or modifying hash) MUST be detected by an independent full verify that does not trust any cached metadata.
normative_clauses.note: 'any modification' includes canonical-form-preserving edits a canonical-bytes hash cannot see (see risks)

normative_clauses.clause: Verify returns a structured verdict
open_choices: verdict representation: dict, NamedTuple, dataclass, custom object; extra fields

normative_clauses.clause: ok=True if every line's recomputed hash matches its stored hash AND every line's stored prev_hash matches the previous line's stored hash.
open_choices: first_bad_index on success (absent / None / other)

normative_clauses.clause: ok=False and first_bad_index=<i> on the first violation.
open_choices: index base (0 or 1)
index of an unparsable line
how the CLI reports the index (unspecified)

normative_clauses.clause: The verify implementation MUST NOT read any field from in-memory state set by append.
normative_clauses.note: a code-structure property; its only consequence (a tamper after the same instance appended is detected) is observable only through the library verdict's representation

normative_clauses.clause: It MUST recompute the chain from disk end-to-end.
This rule applies whether verify is called from CLI or library.
Every mutating operation (put, delete) takes a request id (rid).
open_choices: put/delete/append signatures (argument order, ts parameter, method vs function)

normative_clauses.clause: A rid is a non-empty UTF-8 string supplied by the caller (UUID4, ULID, etc. — format opaque to LedgerLock).
open_choices: behaviour and error type for an empty or non-str rid

normative_clauses.clause: If the same rid is replayed, the second call MUST return the same result
open_choices: replay scope: rid alone (R-4.4/3 implies op-agnostic) vs rid+key
result representation
whether a differing value/ts under the same rid is still a replay

normative_clauses.clause: and MUST NOT append a new line to the chain.
If a different rid tries to mutate a key whose last committed mutation used a different rid, the call MUST raise ConflictError (or return an error result depending on CLI surface)
open_choices: exception attributes and message
conflicts between elements of one batch (earlier element not committed)
the CLI error result's form beyond exit 4

normative_clauses.clause: and MUST NOT append a new line.
A delete produces a tombstone line.
open_choices: value slot of a delete op
delete of a never-put key

normative_clauses.clause: A subsequent put on the same key with a different rid MUST conflict against the tombstone just as it would against a live value.
A subsequent put with the same rid as the tombstone is an idempotent replay and MUST be a no-op returning the same result as the delete.
open_choices: result representation

normative_clauses.clause: A put on key k with rid=r1, then a delete on key k with rid=r2 — the second MUST conflict.
Replays of either MUST NOT conflict.
normative_clauses.note: holds consistently only for the committed put; a replay of the refused delete r2 conflicts again by R-4.3 (see risks)

normative_clauses.clause: apply_batch(ops) accepts an iterable of (op, key, value, rid, ts) tuples
open_choices: method of a path-bound Ledger vs module function

return value (per-op results, count, None)

normative_clauses.clause: under the lock
normative_clauses.note: 'the lock' is never defined; threading/fcntl/msvcrt are outside R-10's allowlist; concurrency is outside every probe's vocabulary

normative_clauses.clause: writes all lines to a sibling temp file, fsyncs the temp file, then renames it over the JSONL path

normative_clauses.clause: If the process crashes at any point, the JSONL on disk MUST either reflect the full batch or be byte-identical to its pre-batch state — never a partial batch.
normative_clauses.note: universal over crash points; see expressibility of R-5 in plan criterion AC-STORY-03-01-5

normative_clauses.clause: The CLI equivalent is ledgerlock apply --batch <file> which reads the batch spec and performs the same atomic operation.

CLI output

normative_clauses.clause: snapshot() returns a deterministic, sorted JSON document representing the current materialized state: for each key, the most recent committed put value (if not tombstoned by a later delete)
open_choices: document layout (object key->value vs list of pairs)
return type (bytes, str, dict)
whitespace, escaping, trailing newline

normative_clauses.clause: sorted by NFC-normalized key in byte order (UTF-8 codepoint order)
The snapshot MUST be byte-stable for a given chain content (same chain → same snapshot bytes).

normative_clauses.clause: If the JSONL ends in a truncated line (last byte is not \n and the last line does not parse / hash), ledgerlock repair-tail MUST rewrite the file with the truncated final line removed

result when the only line is truncated (empty file)

normative_clauses.clause: and verify cleanly afterwards.
No other content may be modified.
If the chain is clean, repair-tail is a no-op.
If the chain is corrupt in the middle (not at the tail), repair-tail MUST refuse.
open_choices: 'refuse' = no write (implied by R-7/3)

normative_clauses.clause: After a successful append, the bytes MUST be durably on disk before the function returns successfully.

normative_clauses.clause: Implementation: write to temp file, fsync, then rename; or open the JSONL in append mode and call f.flush(); os.fsync(fd) before close.

caveats: Under MUST_NOT_HOLD the two REFUTED-by-construction paths (non-UTF-8 file, expired window) become fail-OPEN; under MUST_HOLD {matches: 0} (a prohibition) the same paths are fail-closed. The undecodable path is deterministic per revision and can be closed by a companion MUST_HOLD contract over the same selection with a never-matching pattern such as '(?!)' and {matches: 0} (SATISFIED only when every selected file decodes); the expired-window path of the MUST_NOT_HOLD evaluation itself cannot be closed by another contract.

A 'line' is str.splitlines() of the UTF-8 text (also splits on \r, \x0b, \x0c, \x1c-\x1e, \x85, U+2028, U+2029); each line counts once however many matches it holds; the pattern is Python re with re.search per line, not POSIX ERE.
The tree is read from the git object store at the revision SHA (committed content, never the working file).
The grep text and suffixes pass through the contract's test-artefact filter: 'import unittest' is refused at contract creation; '...|unittest|...' passes.
A textual presence check presumes a spelling (e.g. 'import argparse' vs 'from argparse import ...'); choose patterns that cover every import form.

polarity.rule: A source-tree prohibition is 'the number of product source lines matching the prohibited form is exactly 0': observable {matches: 0, within_s: W}, stimulus {grep: <prohibited form>, suffixes: ['.py']}, subject file_artifact path:ledgerlock, polarity MUST_HOLD (candidate SATISFIED). MUST_NOT_HOLD over {matches: 0} states the opposite ('at least one prohibited line exists') — the inversion recorded as C2-P5-FINDING-001. PLAN-V2.1's MUST_NOT_HOLD label names the prohibited behaviour, whose own observable ('matches >= 1') is not in the vocabulary; its only expressible form is MUST_HOLD over matches == 0.
polarity.subject_absence: REQUIRES_SUBJECT: under ABSENCE_IS_DECIDABLE a missing ledgerlock/ is SUBJECT_ABSENT with the zero-match verdict SATISFIED, a vacuous pass of every prohibition.
polarity.fail_mode: Under MUST_HOLD a non-UTF-8 file or an expired window is REFUTED -> UNSATISFIED (fail-closed); a file with a NUL byte is skipped (fail-open for anything hidden in it; CPython refuses to import source holding NUL, so an importable .py cannot hide there).

requirements.text: A key that has a committed put can never be deleted or changed. R-4.4/3 makes replay op-agnostic (a put with the tombstone's rid replays the delete), so delete(k, r1) after put(k, r1) is a replay (no tombstone), and delete(k, r2) conflicts (R-4.3, R-4.5/1). Keys are write-once; R-6's 'most recent committed put' has one candidate and 'if not tombstoned by a later delete' is unreachable for a put key; tombstones exist only as a key's first mutation. Any spec expecting put-then-delete to remove a key contradicts R-4.

'Replays of either MUST NOT conflict': the delete r2 conflicted and was never committed; replaying it is again a different rid on k, which R-4.3 requires to conflict. Consistent only if 'either' means the committed put.
Replay scope is rid alone (implied by R-4.4/3) or rid+key; under rid alone, put(a, r) then put(b, r) never stores b (affects AC-STORY-02-02-1).

'verify ... Any other exit code is a bug' vs usage error 2 and I/O error 3 (file not found) for verify; with R-14/1 'fresh ledger' read as a nonexistent path, R-9/4 (3) and R-14/1 (0) disagree. Only 'fresh = existing empty file' is consistent.

'Any modification ... MUST be detected' vs a hash over canonical bytes: edits that preserve the canonical form (whitespace, key order, \u00e9 vs literal é, possibly 1.0 vs 1) are undetectable unless canonical bytes equal stored bytes. Only semantic edits are testable.
'The first line's prev_hash is the literal string "GENESIS"' then '(64 hex chars of zeros OR ... implementation choice)'; 'documented' has no location. No neutral spec fixes the value.

R-12/2 forbids opening files other than the ledger, batch input and snapshot output, but R-5/3 (and R-8/2's first strategy) require a sibling temp file, and any file lock for R-5's 'the lock' would be another file. The reference opens a mkstemp sibling.
'under the lock' is undefined; threading/fcntl/msvcrt are not allowed, so it can only be an O_EXCL lock file (in tension with R-12/2) or trivial in-process serialisation.

A newline-terminated last line that fails parse/hash is neither truncated (R-7/1 needs last byte not \n) nor 'in the middle'; R-9/6's exit 5 covers only 'non-tail corruption'. repair-tail's behaviour and exit code for it are unspecified. 'does not parse / hash' is itself ambiguous (OR vs AND).
Conflicts and replays between elements of one batch: R-4.3 judges against the last COMMITTED mutation, and an earlier element of the same batch is not committed.

R-10 requires 'from __future__ import annotations' but __future__ is not in its allowlist; intra-package imports (cli.py -> ledger.py) are not listed either. A literal allowlist check fails every conforming tree.
R-3.2's line shapes omit 'hash' and 'prev_hash', which R-3.2/3 and R-3.3 require on every line.
append/verify/snapshot/apply_batch as module functions or methods; put/delete/append signatures and ts provenance unspecified; apply_batch(ops) and snapshot() read as methods of a path-bound Ledger.
Durability, crash-at-any-point atomicity, 'does not read in-memory state', file-access confinement and the interpreter version are outside every probe's vocabulary.
'0 — success (append ...)' names a CLI append that no clause specifies (only apply --batch).
'No third-party imports succeed at runtime' reads as an environment property, not a tree property.

synthetic_approval.approver_shape: ContractApproval.approver must be a str that starts with 'human:' and has a non-blank remainder (approval.py HUMAN_PREFIX; __post_init__: approver.startswith('human:') and approver[6:].strip()); anything else — a model or agent identity included — raises ContractError. The other fields: requirement_id + requirement_hash + contract_id + contract_hash (all bound by binding_problems), approved_at a finite int/float (not bool), model_reviews a tuple of str (advisory journal references only).
synthetic_approval.what_the_check_is: Purely syntactic. No registry, signature, owner list or provenance is consulted: 'human:owner' and 'human:c2-p5-proposal-check' are indistinguishable to the kernel. require_approved accepts any approval whose four ids/hashes match the current requirement and contract.
why_never_persist_a_synthetic_identity: A persisted ContractApproval with a synthetic 'human:...' approver bound to a real contract_hash and requirement_hash passes require_approved exactly as the owner's would, so compile_spec (and the static admission engine) would produce and admit a ProductProofSpec on authority that RFC §6 reserves to a human.
Nothing downstream can tell it apart later: the approver string is the only authority evidence and it is free text after the prefix; approved_at is not checked against anything.
It does not expire: it stays valid for as long as the two bound hashes do, i.e. it silently authorises that exact contract forever.
